links.targetTitle: Made Tech — Delivers under the UK Technology Code of Practice, which MANDATES open source

title: Made Tech delivers in the one market where publishing source is a contractual obligation
content:
Made Tech's open-source posture is not a preference it could revise; it is a term of the market it sells into. The firm delivers under the UK Technology Code of Practice, which mandates open source by default for new government code, so publishing the source is an obligation on the work rather than a cultural choice by the supplier.

That distinction changes how a partnership conversation opens. With most leads the screening question is whether a stated openness survives contact with a client's procurement. Here the procurement is what creates the openness, and a supplier operating under a default-open mandate has already absorbed the licensing, review and disclosure overhead that other firms treat as project risk.

The caveat in the record is precise: the mandate is verified, the firm's own contributions were not individually checked. What is established is the regime it works under, not a portfolio of repositories. At 433 people in the UK it sits at priority 2.
